data.name: Super Perspective
data.detailed_description:
Super Perspective is a mind-bending puzzle platformer where you can switch between 2D and 3D at will to solve puzzles and explore! Gather crystals with the help of your cheeky guide and find your way home!

Features:
* Use your command over perspective to traverse obstacles in new and creative ways!
* Travel through multiple worlds with unique mechanics in search of big crystals!
* Every level has optional small crystal puzzles! Are you up to the challenge?
* Stuck on a tricky puzzle? Consult your local crystal fairy for hints!

Note: Xbox 360 controller is fully supported after the game has launched from the launcher.

reviews.review:
Super Perspective is a small puzzle platformer that does something I do not see very often. I can switch between 2D and 3D perspective while moving through each level, and I have to use that change in perspective to reach areas that I could not normally get to. The basic idea is easy enough to understand, but it takes a little while before I start seeing the levels in the way the game expects me to. I am basically looking at the same space in two different ways and trying to figure out how I can use that to get around an obstacle.

The perspective switching is easily the best part for me. Some sections look impossible until I realise that changing the view makes a platform line up in a completely different way. I like that feeling because the solution usually comes from understanding the level rather than simply having better platforming skills. There are three main worlds with their own themes and mechanics, including the forest, desert and ice areas, and each one gives me a slightly different way to use the main idea. The game also gives me big crystals to collect, which gives each area a clear goal.

I also like that I can go looking for the smaller crystals. They are optional, so I do not have to collect everything just to finish the levels, but they give me a reason to explore places I might otherwise ignore. Some of them are tucked into awkward spots where I have to properly understand the perspective mechanic rather than just walking through the level. I enjoy this because the main path lets me keep moving forward while the extra collectibles give me something harder to work towards when I want to test myself.

The game is not completely about puzzles either. There is still some platforming involved, so I have to move carefully and judge jumps while I am also thinking about how the perspective works. That can make some sections more frustrating than I expect because I am trying to solve the puzzle and perform the movement at the same time. The game does have a crystal fairy that can give me hints when I get stuck, which I appreciate because some of the solutions can take a while to spot. I would rather have the option to get a small nudge than be completely stuck on one section.

The biggest weakness for me is the amount of content. Super Perspective is free and there are three main themed worlds, but it is still a fairly small game. Once I understand how its perspective system works, there are only so many new tricks it can introduce before I have seen most of what it has to offer. I would have liked more worlds or a few more complicated mechanics towards the end because the main idea has enough potential for a much bigger game. The presentation is also fairly simple, although I think the clean style works well enough for a puzzle game where I need to clearly see what I am doing.

I do like the atmosphere though. The forest, desert and ice areas give the game some visual variety, and the soundtrack has separate music for the main menu, hub, tutorial, worlds and other sections. It is not a huge production, but it gives the game enough character that it does not feel like a bare puzzle prototype. There are also eight achievements, including goals for collecting all the crystals and completing each world, which gives me a little extra reason to go back and finish everything properly.

Overall, Super Perspective is a clever little game built around a genuinely good puzzle idea. I like switching between 2D and 3D, working out how perspective changes the levels and searching for the optional crystals. The main thing holding it back for me is that the idea is better than the amount of content available, and some sections can be awkward when the platforming and puzzle solving are happening at the same time. Still, it is completely free, easy to understand and different enough from a normal platformer that I think it is well worth trying. It is a small game, but there is a good idea at its centre and I think the developer gets a lot out of it.

Rating: 7.4/10
